name: TX-08
label: Likely R

model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean and Steinmann's overwhelming financial advantage over a barely funded Democratic opponent point to a comfortable Republican hold, and markets price the race at roughly 95% Republican. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic spending or an unexpected Steinmann scandal could narrow the margin, though the district's lean makes an upset unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Morgan Luttrell (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
TX-08 is an open Republican-held seat north of Houston, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward the GOP after Morgan Luttrell's retirement. Republican Jessica Hart Steinmann enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised over $2 million and benefited from roughly $1.7 million in outside support, while Democrat Laura Jones has raised only about $22,000 with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets put Republican chances near 95%. The seat remains Likely Republican, with the main uncertainty coming from the open-seat dynamic rather than any visible Democratic strength.
